rules.detail: The policy regulates only 'buying and selling company securities issued by the company', where securities means shares, company-issued options and other company-issued securities. It contains no dealing definition sweeping in third-party derivatives, agreements to deal, or financial products referencing the shares, so an OTC put or call written by a bank is not addressed.
Hedging is not mentioned anywhere in the policy, including in relation to option plan securities.
Monetisation arrangements such as prepaid forwards are not mentioned.
Short selling is not mentioned; the policy addresses only buying and selling of company securities held by the person.
CFDs and other exchange-traded derivatives over the company's securities are not mentioned.
Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over the company's securities is not mentioned and is not captured by the policy's narrow focus on buying and selling.
Secured financing arrangements of any kind are not mentioned or restricted.

The policy expresses an aspiration to long-term holding and discourages short-term trading, but imposes no defined minimum holding period, buy/sell window, or intention test, and no consequence is stated for short-term dealing that otherwise complies with the trading windows and clearance procedure.
rules.evidence: This policy encourages directors, officers, and employees to be long-term holders of the company's securities, and discourages short-term trading.

exceptions.evidence: Directors, officers, or employees participating, or eligible to participate, in the company's share option plan are permitted to: 1. Accept an invitation to participate in a grant of options under the plan; 2. Exercise options to acquire Select Harvests' securities (as applicable) under the plan; and 3. Exercise any other action or right permitted under the plan, at any time, whether or not the above actions occur within the trading windows specified above.

Directors, officers, or employees who desire to receive payment of directors' fees or salary by way of shares in lieu of cash are permitted to make an election in writing to receive payment by the purchase of shares on the share market ... An election made within a trading window to receive payment by shares in lieu of cash must be for a minimum period of 12 months.

exceptions.evidence: If there are exceptional circumstances and the person concerned declares that they do not possess any unpublished price sensitive information, the applicable Notification Officer may, after consulting with, and obtaining approval from, the Chairman, allow an officer, or employee to sell company securities outside a trading window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The company's share trading policy regulates dealings by directors, officers, and employees, in shares, options and other securities issued by the company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy only restricts buying and selling of company-issued securities; it contains no sweep-up definition of 'dealing' catching derivatives, encumbrances or financing arrangements, so a bank-written OTC put/call and a loan secured on the shares fall outside its express scope.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buying and selling company securities by directors, officers, and employees outside the above trading window is prohibited.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any step that does involve buying or selling the underlying shares (e.g. physical delivery on collar unwind or default) would need to occur within one of the four scheduled windows or the Board-permitted 'Other' period, or require the exceptional-circumstances sign-off.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Board discretion to open extra periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Other: At any such other times as the Board of Directors of the company permits.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Board can create an additional open period at its discretion, giving flexibility to time collar execution or unwind outside the four scheduled windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: each director has agreed to provide notice of such dealings to the company within five business days of any such dealing to enable the company to comply with its corresponding obligation to notify the ASX.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any share movement a director makes in connection with the collar (e.g. delivering shares on settlement) must be reported to the company within five business days for Appendix 3Y purposes, even though the collar derivatives themselves are not covered by the policy.

summary: This is a short, older-style policy that regulates only the buying and selling of shares, company-issued options and other company-issued securities within four scheduled trading windows (or a Board-permitted 'Other' period), subject to prior written approval from the relevant Notification Officer. It contains no definition of 'dealing' that sweeps in derivatives, hedging, encumbrance, stock lending or secured financing, and none of those topics, nor margin lending, short selling or CFDs, is mentioned anywhere in the document. On its face, therefore, nothing in the policy expressly prohibits a director or executive from entering an OTC put/call collar with a bank or granting security over vested shares to secure a loan, since these are not 'buying or selling' company securities. Caution is still warranted: any actual transfer or sale of shares connected with entry, unwind or default under the collar would need to occur within an open trading window (or under the exceptional-circumstances carve-out with Chairman/Board approval) and, for directors, must be reported to the company within five business days for ASX notification purposes. Because the policy is silent rather than permissive by design, the bank should also confirm current market practice and any unwritten insider-trading overlay before relying on this silence.
